english.title: Interfere with / obstruct / mislead / impede police or member of HM Forces in vicinity of prohibited place
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), in the vicinity of a prohibited place, namely **(..SPECIFY PROHIBITED PLACE..),

(A)_[obstructed]_
(B)_[knowingly misled]_
(C)_[interfered with or impeded]_

**(..SPECIFY PERSON OBSTRUCTED, MISLED, INTERFERED WITH OR IMPEDED..),

(D)_[the chief officer of police who was]_
(E)_[a superintendent of police]_
(F)_[a police officer]_
(G)_[a member of His Majesty's Forces]_

engaged on guard, sentry, patrol or other similar duty in relation to the prohibited place
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 3 and 8(2) of the Official Secrets Act 1920.

english.notes:
(i) Whilst this offence is triable either way, it should usually be dealt with on indictment. The offence may only be dealt with summarily with the consent of the Attorney General (section 8(2) Official Secrets Act 1920).
(ii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
